learning.objective: Practice separating media authenticity from claim veracity and context integrity when a real-looking flood image is shared with an urgent caption.
learning.priorKnowledge: Learners know that images can be reposted outside their original time and place.
learning.likelyMisconception: If a photo looks authentic, the caption must be trustworthy.
learning.responsibleSharingGoal: Do not amplify an urgent claim until source, date, place, and independent context are checked.

presentation.claim: Breaking: central Munich is flooding right now after a dam failure, with hundreds injured.
presentation.context: A dramatic flood image appears in a fast-moving group chat. The caption asks people to repost immediately.

media.altText: A street-level flood scene with cars partly submerged and people standing near high water.

presentation.initialConfidencePrompt: Before investigating, how confident are you that the caption is accurate?
presentation.conclusionPrompt: After checking evidence, assess the image, the claim, and the context separately.

evidenceActions.label: Check original poster
evidenceActions.description: Inspect whether the account is the original source or only reposting an unattributed image.

limitations: A repost alone does not prove the claim false, but it weakens source identity.

evidenceActions.label: Scan provenance
evidenceActions.description: Check whether the image has preserved origin metadata or content credentials.

limitations: Metadata supports origin history, not whether the caption is true.

hintLadder.text: What would you need to know before reposting an urgent image like this?
Try separating the image from the caption. Which part can be checked first?
A real image can still be reused with a wrong time or place. Trace the earliest source.
The reviewed source packet points to an older Riverbend City context, so check whether the Munich caption has independent support.
After conclusion, compare your axes: the image can be authentic while the caption's time and place are misleading.

processLevels.criteria: Concludes from instinct or visual appearance only.
Checks source identity or provenance but does not test context.
Finds the earlier source or date/place mismatch.
Corroborates context independently and separates media from caption.
Makes a calibrated three-axis conclusion and chooses a responsible share decision.

rubric.confidenceCalibration: Reward justified confidence updates when learners move from visual certainty to evidence-based uncertainty or correction.

riskNotes: Avoid using real victims or live emergency claims in the P0 demo.
Do not imply this fixture is a live Munich incident.
privacyNotes: No private people, names, faces, or live user uploads are stored.
